title: The solar neighbourhood: 1,570 Gaia DR3 stars with radial velocities

reductions: The cuts: RUWE below 1.4 (Gaia's flag for a poor astrometric solution), a parallax measured to more than 10 times its error (so that 1/parallax is a distance to 10 percent or better), and a Gaia radial velocity.

Two strata of the stars that pass those cuts, each a random subset chosen by Gaia's own random_index: the nearer 489 stars (parallax above 10 mas, closer than 100 pc) are about 1 in 273 of the 133,468 that pass; the remaining 1081 (parallax 1 to 10 mas, 100 pc to 1 kpc) are about 1 in 9,065 of the 9,798,805. The proportions are not the sky's: the near stratum is over-sampled so that the Sun's motion has stars near enough to be measured without the Galaxy's rotation in them.
Gaia measures radial velocities only for stars brighter than about G_RVS = 14, which favours bright stars; the sample is not volume-complete and its colours are not those of the stellar population.
No parallax zero-point correction is applied (Lindegren et al. 2021 give about -0.017 mas on average: 1.7 percent at 100 pc, 1.7 percent at 1 kpc to the distance).

Positions are rounded to 0.006 degree in right ascension and 0.004 degree in declination (22 and 14 arcsec), parallaxes to 0.02 mas, proper motions to 0.01 mas/yr, radial velocities to 0.02 km/s: good for Galactic coordinates to 0.01 degree and for velocities to under 0.1 km/s, not for a cross-match.
Galactic longitude and latitude are not stored: the galactic kernel computes them from the position, and its transformation is tested against the values Gaia's archive gives.
The Gaia source ids are left out (a 64-bit id does not fit the table encoding); the query in the pack's manifest returns them, and the rows are in its order.

Version 1.1.0 adds eight columns to the same 1,570 rows, all stored to the step shown: the three error correlations, RUWE, the solution type, the effective wavenumber or pseudocolour (each empty for the other solution type), and the ecliptic latitude. Every earlier column is identical to version 1.0.0 (tests/fixtures/gaia-workflows/alignment.json holds its checksum). The parallax is still rounded to 0.02 mas: this pack is not used for a distance, because that rounding is as large as the parallax error of its far stratum.

queries: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_error, pmra, pmra_error, pmdec, pmdec_error, radial_velocity, radial_velocity_error, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax_pmra_corr, parallax_pmdec_corr, pmra_pmdec_corr, ruwe, astrometric_params_solved, nu_eff_used_in_astrometry, pseudocolour, ecl_lat FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE ruwe<1.4 AND radial_velocity IS NOT NULL AND parallax_over_error>10 AND ((parallax>10 AND random_index<7000000) OR (parallax>1 AND parallax<=10 AND random_index<200000)) ORDER BY source_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE ruwe<1.4 AND radial_velocity IS NOT NULL AND parallax_over_error>10 AND parallax>10
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE ruwe<1.4 AND radial_velocity IS NOT NULL AND parallax_over_error>10 AND parallax>1 AND parallax<=10

steps: Query Gaia DR3 for stars with RUWE below 1.4, a radial velocity and a parallax measured to better than 10 sigma, taking the random subset random_index < 7,000,000 of those with parallax above 10 mas and random_index < 200,000 of those with parallax 1 to 10 mas, ordered by source id.
Count, in two further queries, every star passing the cuts in each stratum, for the sampling fractions.
Encode as table-columns/1: each column a whole number of its step from an offset, int16 where the range fits.

assumptions: Distance is 1/parallax with no zero-point correction and no prior; at parallax over error above 10 that is accurate to 10 percent or better, and the bias from the omitted correction is stated above.
The Sun is at the origin; velocities are heliocentric until a student subtracts the Sun's motion.

validation.check: the kernel's solar motion from the stars within 100 pc has U and W within 3 km/s of Schonrich, Binney and Dehnen 2010
